solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Light yellow pastry lined with cross base (6)

indicators.note: the pastry has the other letters set inside it, like a lining

blocks.note: a flan is an open pastry case
X is the shape of a cross
e is the base of natural logarithms

annotation.surface: A baker describes a pale golden tart with a crossed pattern on its base.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pastry sounds like a recipe, but 'cross' and 'base' are two separate one-letter pieces tucked inside FLAN.
annotation.definitionFit: Flaxen is the pale yellow colour of flax fibre, usually said of hair.

entries.clue: By the sound of it, purchase paper boat (6)

indicators.note: tells you the wordplay is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: buy = purchase, a ream = a quantity of paper

annotation.surface: Someone buying paper to make a paper boat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Paper boat' looks like one thing, a child's folded toy; it splits so that 'paper' ends the wordplay and 'boat' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A bireme is an ancient galley with two banks of oars.

entries.clue: They’d invoiced me for work, work from ages ago (3,6,6)

indicators.note: the letters are to be worked, reshaped into something new

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

annotation.surface: A freelancer grumbles that a client billed them for a job done long ago.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Work' appears twice with two jobs: the first is the instruction to rearrange, the second is the definition, a literary work.
annotation.definitionFit: The Divine Comedy is Dante's fourteenth-century poem, a work from centuries ago.

entries.clue: Outlet for water monster nymphet drained (7)

indicators.note: the word is emptied of its middle, leaving its outside letters

blocks.note: the many-headed monster of Greek myth
NYMPHET with its inside emptied out

annotation.surface: A water monster and a nymph, straight out of a myth about a spring.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Water monster' reads as one creature; 'water' belongs to the definition and HYDRA comes from 'monster' alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A hydrant is a street pipe with a nozzle from which water can be drawn.

entries.clue: As Dorothy was in The Wizard of Oz film (4,4,3,4)

annotation.definition2: As Dorothy was in The Wizard of Oz

blocks.clueFragment: As Dorothy was in The Wizard of Oz
blocks.note: a tornado carries Dorothy and her house away to Oz
the 1939 epic

annotation.surface: A film quiz question about Dorothy in The Wizard of Oz.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like it completes 'The Wizard of Oz film', but it is a separate definition: a different 1939 film entirely.
annotation.definitionFit: Gone with the Wind is the 1939 film, released the same year as The Wizard of Oz.

entries.clue: Student entering criticises doctor about unwelcome temperature (4,4)

indicators.note: the student goes into the other letters
about means turned around, so the combined letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: pans = criticises harshly, as a reviewer does
doc = doctor
L = learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

annotation.surface: A student walks in on someone laying into a doctor over a bad fever.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Temperature' pulls towards a fever, which is what the doctor seems to be blamed for; the definition is weather instead.
annotation.definitionFit: A cold snap is a sudden short spell of cold weather, an unwelcome drop in temperature.

entries.clue: Dangerous split upset equities saver, crashing stocks (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards
the words stock the answer, holding it inside them

blocks.note: the letters hiding across the three words

annotation.surface: A market report: a saver's equities crash as stocks split.
annotation.walkthrough: The finance words are all packaging: the answer sits backwards across 'equitiES SAVER Crashing'.
annotation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep crack in a glacier, a split that climbers can fall into.

entries.clue: Irresistible burning yen to embrace maiden (8)

indicators.note: the other letters hug the maiden, putting her inside

blocks.note: alight = on fire
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen
M = maiden, a maiden over in cricket scoring

annotation.surface: A burning, irresistible longing to hold a young woman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Burning yen' reads as a fierce desire; here yen is only the currency letter Y.
annotation.definitionFit: Almighty means all-powerful, so impossible to resist.

entries.clue: Smells good, our sausage sandwiches! (6)

indicators.note: the words hold the answer between them, like bread round a filling

blocks.note: the letters run from the second letter of 'good' to the first of 'sausage'

annotation.surface: Someone sniffing appreciatively at sausage sandwiches cooking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sausage sandwiches' reads as a snack; 'sandwiches' is the verb, holding the answer inside the words before it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are nouns for scents, pleasant or not.

entries.clue: Racket and ball taken from revered Norseman (3)

indicators.note: the ball is removed from the name

blocks.note: Odin, chief god of Norse myth
O is round like a ball

annotation.surface: A tennis racket and ball being taken from a Viking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Racket and ball' reads as sports kit; racket is the noise, and only the ball is used in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words mean loud, confused noise.

entries.clue: Something that’ll stretch former nurse? (8)

blocks.note: ex = former
a tender is one who tends, a nurse

annotation.surface: A riddle about what a retired nurse would call a stretcher.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Former nurse' feels like a retired person; it is two pieces, EX and TENDER. The question mark flags the playful definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An extender is anything that lengthens or stretches something else.

entries.clue: US chicory tips from Euston bar (6)

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends

blocks.note: the first and last letters of EUSTON
a dive is a seedy bar

annotation.surface: An American visitor buys salad greens from a bar at Euston, a London railway station.
annotation.walkthrough: In the US 'endive' names the chicory Britons call chicory, which is why the definition is flagged as American.
annotation.definitionFit: Americans call the pale forced chicory head an endive.

entries.clue: Innovation is, for Germans, about odd bits of theory for meddling in the economy (15)

indicators.note: the innovation goes round the next piece
take the letters in odd positions

blocks.note: an invention is an innovation
letters 1, 3 and 5 of THEORY
ist is German for 'is'

annotation.surface: A commentator on how German economists view innovation and state meddling.
annotation.walkthrough: IST comes at the end although the clue mentions it second: it is simply placed after the finished container.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: interventionist policy has the state step into markets, which its critics call meddling.

entries.clue: Jerk, belly up (3)

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: gut = belly

annotation.surface: An insult: someone is a jerk with a belly on show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Belly up' suggests something dead or bust; 'up' is only the instruction to reverse.
annotation.definitionFit: A tug is a sudden sharp pull, a jerk.

entries.clue: Swell chaps sitting in gold sports car (7)

indicators.note: the chaps are seated inside the car

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
GT = gran turismo, a sports car
chaps = men

annotation.surface: Well-to-do chaps lounging in a gold sports car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swell chaps' reads as posh fellows; 'Swell' is the verb and the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: To augment is to swell, making something bigger.

entries.clue: Fearless United supporter repelled attack (8)

indicators.note: driven back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: U = United, as in football club names
FAN turned back
a raid is an attack

annotation.surface: A brave Manchester United fan fights off an attack.
annotation.walkthrough: The football story is the disguise; 'United' is just the U used in team abbreviations such as Man U.
annotation.definitionFit: Unafraid means without fear, fearless.

entries.clue: Husband in combat injured by incendiary equipment (8)

indicators.note: the husband goes inside the other letters
the word is damaged, its letters knocked about

blocks.note: H = husband, as in family trees
anagram fodder
X is the multiplication sign, read 'by' as in 3 by 4

annotation.surface: A husband wounded in battle by a firebomb.
annotation.walkthrough: COMBAT is rearranged to MATCBO with H inside; 'by' is not a link but X, the times sign in dimensions like 2 by 4.
annotation.definitionFit: A matchbox holds matches, equipment for lighting fires.

entries.clue: Wreath quietly laid in Swiss Cottage? (7)

indicators.note: put inside the other word

blocks.note: p = piano, quietly in music
a chalet is a cottage in Switzerland; the question mark marks the definition by example

annotation.surface: A wreath quietly laid at Swiss Cottage, a district of north London, as at a memorial.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swiss Cottage' is a real London place name with a tube station; read literally it is a Swiss cottage, a chalet.
annotation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a wreath or garland worn on the head.

entries.clue: Something like 18 Across that is left over (3)

indicators.note: turned over, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: i.e. = id est, that is
L = left

annotation.surface: Something left over, like the wreath from the previous clue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left over' looks like leftovers; the two words split, one the letter L and one the reversing instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers, a kind of wreath like a chaplet.

entries.clue: Head brought up chatter showing what a student might be on? (7)

annotation.definition: what a student might be on?

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: bean = head, informally
gab = chatter

annotation.surface: A tutor wonders what a student is on, suspecting drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'What a student might be on' suggests drugs or a grant; the answer is the floppy seat students sit on.
annotation.definitionFit: A beanbag is a large soft seat, a staple of student rooms.

entries.clue: Playing I-spy, Carl pitches tricky subject (8,7)

indicators.note: the letters are played with, rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

annotation.surface: A boy named Carl playing I-spy suggests a very hard thing to spot.
annotation.walkthrough: Carl seems to be a person playing a game; his name is only letters for the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: Particle physics studies subatomic particles, a famously difficult subject.

entries.clue: Top copper: “Bravo, magnificent!” (6)

blocks.note: super = superintendent, a senior police officer
Bravo is B in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A senior police officer congratulating someone on a great result.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is British slang for a police officer, and a 'super' is a superintendent.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words praise something as outstandingly fine.

entries.clue: Credit initially after tax for menswear item (6)

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: CR = credit, in accounts
first letter of AFTER
VAT = value added tax, the UK sales tax

annotation.surface: A tax receipt, with credit applied, for a tie.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Credit initially' seems to ask for C; 'initially' applies to the next word, 'after', giving A.
annotation.definitionFit: A cravat is a scarf-like neckband worn by men.

entries.clue: American navy edge battle (6)

blocks.note: A = American
RN = Royal Navy
a hem is an edge of cloth

annotation.surface: An American navy edging into battle.
annotation.walkthrough: The navy is the British Royal Navy even though it follows 'American'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Dutch town gave its name to the 1944 airborne battle fought there.

entries.clue: The latest summit contribution from Blair? (8)

blocks.note: the news is the latest
a peak is a summit

annotation.surface: Tony Blair's latest remarks at a political summit.
annotation.walkthrough: Blair points to Tony Blair, but it is Eric Blair, George Orwell's real name; Newspeak is the language of his 1984.
annotation.definitionFit: Orwell coined Newspeak, so it is his contribution to the language.

entries.clue: English King in decline (3)

blocks.note: E = English
B.B. King, the American blues guitarist

annotation.surface: An English monarch in decline.
annotation.walkthrough: 'English King' looks like a royal; the king is B.B. King the bluesman, and 'in' is only a link.
annotation.definitionFit: To ebb is to decline, like a tide going out.

entries.clue: Mike regularly used Hilltop Road, an upper-class address (6)

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is used

blocks.note: Mike is M in the NATO alphabet
letters 2, 4 and 6 of HILLTOP
Rd = Road

annotation.surface: Mike regularly drives along Hilltop Road, a posh street address.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Address' suggests a street, which Hilltop Road seems to be; it is a form of address, a way of speaking to a lord.
annotation.definitionFit: Milord is an old way of addressing an English nobleman.

entries.clue: Weird rating given to opera opening in London (8)

indicators.note: the first letter of the word

blocks.note: AB = able seaman, a naval rating
Bellini's opera Norma
first letter of LONDON

annotation.surface: A strange review score for an opera opening in London.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rating' sounds like a review score; it is a sailor, and 'opera opening' is not one phrase: 'opening' belongs to London.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something weird departs from the normal, which is exactly what the answer says.
